name: oilliphéist
text: oilliphéist is a dragon-like monster from Irish oral tradition, named from the Irish words oil meaning great and prist meaning fabulous beast or reptile. In the best-known story, the oilliphéist dams the watercourse of the Shannon River on hearing that Saint Patrick has arrived to expel its kind from the land. In a comic sequel, the monster swallows a drunken piper who keeps playing inside it until the creature coughs him up. The Scottish Gaelic counterpart is uilepheist. The wider tradition also names related monsters caoránach, muirdris, and sinach.

attributes.attribute: Irish dragon-like monster that dams the Shannon against Saint Patrick
